newsitem.title: GERMANY: Jochimsen-BoE changes still not enough for EMU.
newsitem.headline: Jochimsen-BoE changes still not enough for EMU.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Reimut Jochimsen said on Monday that Britain's move to increase the independence of the Bank of England did not on its own mean that Britain had made a fundamental step towards joining EMU.

"It was a brave and quick decision but it doesn't give the Bank of England the level of independence required by the Maastricht treaty," Jochimsen, who is also president of the state bank of North Rhine-Westphalia, told a news conference.

Last week's decision by Britain's new Labour government to give the central bank independence to set interest rates meant that Britain would fulfil one of the conditions for European Economic and Monetary Union.
He also said that last week's U.K. interest rate rise demonstrated the decisiveness of the new Labour government.
Referring to the increase in the Bank of England's independence, Jochimsen said: "Basic interests have not been changed. It is much too early to draw conclusions from this."
